title: Tensor transition and complete-intersection fibre comparison after scalar extension
statement:
Let $R_0\to R_k\xrightarrow{\alpha}R_j$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings, let $B_0,C_0$ be commutative $R_0$-algebras, and let $\varphi_0:B_0\to C_0$ be an $R_0$-algebra homomorphism. For $t=k,j$ put $B_t=R_t\otimes_{R_0}B_0$, $C_t=R_t\otimes_{R_0}C_0$ and $\varphi_t=1\otimes\varphi_0:B_t\to C_t$; use the maps induced by $\alpha$ for the transition from $k$ to $j$. Assume $\varphi_k$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and that for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset B_k$ the fibre $C_k\otimes_{B_k}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a local complete intersection over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Then the following hold.
There is a $B_j$-algebra isomorphism
$$\theta:B_j\otimes_{B_k}C_k\xrightarrow{\sim}C_j,\qquad (r\otimes b)\otimes(s\otimes c)\longmapsto r\alpha(s)\otimes\varphi_0(b)c,$$
whose inverse sends $r\otimes c$ to $(r\otimes1)\otimes(1\otimes c)$. Under $\theta$, $\varphi_j$ is the map $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. For every prime $\mathfrak q\subset B_j$, its inverse image $\mathfrak p\subset B_k$ is prime and the induced field homomorphism $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ gives a $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$-algebra isomorphism
$$C_j\otimes_{B_j}\kappa(\mathfrak q)\ \cong\ (C_k\otimes_{B_k}\kappa(\mathfrak p))\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\kappa(\mathfrak q),$$
compatible with the canonical maps from $C_k$ and $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. The algebra $C_k\otimes_{B_k}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is of finite type over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. The map $\varphi_j$ is flat and of finite presentation, and for every prime $\mathfrak q\subset B_j$ its fibre $C_j\otimes_{B_j}\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is a local complete intersection over $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. No flatness or finite-presentation assumption on $\alpha$ or on $R_0\to B_0$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 00SN (lemma-base-change-syntomic), proof, with definition-lci expanded; tensor and residue-field comparison as displayed in the preceding lemma-syntomic-descends. The two iterated-base-change maps are stated explicitly.

proof.text: Write $\beta:B_k\to B_j$ and $\gamma:C_k\to C_j$ for the transition maps. The two maps $\varphi_j:B_j\to C_j$ and $\gamma:C_k\to C_j$ agree on $B_k$: on $s\otimes b$ both give $\alpha(s)\otimes\varphi_0(b)$. The tensor pushout property therefore gives $\theta(x\otimes y)=\varphi_j(x)\gamma(y)$, hence the displayed formula. The compatible maps $R_j\to B_j\otimes_{B_k}C_k$, $r\mapsto(r\otimes1)\otimes1$, and $C_0\to B_j\otimes_{B_k}C_k$, $c\mapsto1\otimes(1\otimes c)$, give a ring map $\eta:C_j\to B_j\otimes_{B_k}C_k$ with the stated inverse formula. It is $B_j$-linear: $1\otimes(1\otimes\varphi_0(b))=(1\otimes b)\otimes1$ by balancing over $B_k$.

source.place: Tags 00CV/00CX (section-tensor-product, lemma-tensor-product), tensor universal property; comparison implicit in Tag 00SN (lemma-base-change-syntomic).

proof.text: The composites are identities on pure tensors. First $\theta\eta(r\otimes c)=r\otimes c$. For the other composite, balancing over $B_k$ gives $((r\otimes b)\otimes(s\otimes c))=(r\alpha(s)\otimes1)\otimes(1\otimes\varphi_0(b)c)$, which is exactly its image under $\eta\theta$. Pure tensors generate, so these are inverse ring maps. Also $\theta(x\otimes1)=\varphi_j(x)$, proving the asserted identification of the structure map.

source.place: Tags 00CV/00CX, tensor balancing relations, and Tag 00SN (lemma-base-change-syntomic).

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B_j$ and set $\mathfrak p=\beta^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. It is proper since $\beta(1)=1\notin\mathfrak q$, and $ab\in\mathfrak p$ implies $\beta(a)\beta(b)\in\mathfrak q$, hence $a\in\mathfrak p$ or $b\in\mathfrak p$. The composite $B_k\to B_j\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ has kernel $\mathfrak p$, by the kernel clause of the residue-field lemma. Every element outside $\mathfrak p$ has nonzero, hence invertible, image. Its factorization clause gives the unique map $\iota:\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ compatible with $B_k$. A unital map between fields is injective, since its kernel cannot contain $1$.

source.place: Local rings, paragraph after Tag 07BI (definition-local-ring), induced map of residue fields; Tag 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient).

proof.text: Put $K=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ and $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Apply tensor cancellation first over $B_k\to B_j\to K$, using $\theta$, and then over $B_k\to k\to K$. With the symmetry $a\otimes b\mapsto b\otimes a$ (whose inverse is the same balanced map), these yield $C_j\otimes_{B_j}K\cong C_k\otimes_{B_k}K\cong(C_k\otimes_{B_k}k)\otimes_kK$. Explicitly, after replacing $C_j$ by $B_j\otimes_{B_k}C_k$, the comparison is $(x\otimes c)\otimes\lambda\mapsto(c\otimes1)\otimes\overline{x}\lambda$; its inverse is $(c\otimes a)\otimes\lambda\mapsto(1\otimes c)\otimes\iota(a)\lambda$. Here $\overline{x}$ is the residue of $x\in B_j$ in $K$. These formulas follow from the cancellation formulas and show that $c\in C_k$ maps to $(c\otimes1)\otimes1$ and $\lambda\in K$ to $(1\otimes1)\otimes\lambda$. Thus both required canonical maps are preserved.

source.place: Tag 00SM (lemma-syntomic-descends), displayed residue-fibre identity; Tag 00D2 (lemma-tensor-with-bimodule), tensor cancellation.

proof.text: Apply flat module base change to $B_k\to B_j$ and the flat $B_k$-module $C_k$. The result is flat over $B_j$, and the $B_j$-linear isomorphism $\theta$ identifies it with $C_j$, so $\varphi_j$ is flat. Apply clause (1) of finite-presentation base change to the same rings: $B_j\to B_j\otimes_{B_k}C_k$ is of finite presentation. Composing its presentation isomorphism with $\theta$ gives a presentation of $C_j$ over $B_j$. Separately, applying clause (1) to $B_k\to k$ shows that $k\otimes_{B_k}C_k$ is finitely presented over $k$. Swapping tensor factors gives the same assertion for $A=C_k\otimes_{B_k}k$. A finite presentation has finitely many algebra generators by its definition, so $A$ is of finite type over $k$.

By hypothesis $A=C_k\otimes_{B_k}k$ is a local complete intersection over $k$. Step 5 verifies the finite-type hypothesis of the field-change lemma, and step 3 supplies the field extension $k\to K$. That lemma implies $A\otimes_kK$ is a local complete intersection over $K$. The $K$-algebra isomorphism of step 4 identifies this algebra with $C_j\otimes_{B_j}K$. Pull the defining principal-open generators across this $K$-algebra isomorphism. The induced localization isomorphisms carry each polynomial presentation to a presentation of the corresponding localization; their bijections on prime ideals preserve chains and therefore Krull dimension. Thus the transported principal opens form a cover with the same global complete-intersection presentations and dimensions, proving that the latter algebra is a local complete intersection too (including the zero-ring convention). This holds for every $\mathfrak q$. Every base-change result used allows an arbitrary base ring map; no flatness of $\alpha$ or finite presentation of $R_0\to B_0$ entered.
